routing_warnings.description: The additional eight-addressable-LED board is an independently defined peripheral board rather than a change to the core power/main/sensor partition.
The three-board power-chain observation primarily defines power forwarding through the main board.
The detailed sensor-board input and module connector specification belongs to the sensor connector-hub Requirement.
The message concerns flexibility in physical connector placement after adoption of the integrated-board variant.
The requested continuity and via-stitching checks concern current-carrying capacity of VBUS and BAT− rather than the power-board layer-count decision.
The observed unstable L3 voltage is runtime evidence about power-rail regulation, not the power-board layer stack.
This message specifies the physical placement and alignment of connectors on the main and sensor boards rather than the main-board outline or routing capacity.
The hard requirement to retain access to every ESP32 pin belongs to the independent full-pin-breakout Requirement.
The clause requiring the ESP32-S3 antenna to face away from the battery with a minimum 3 mm keepout belongs to the separate antenna-clearance Requirement.
This message evaluates components located in the ESP32 antenna clear area and should be routed to the antenna-clearance Requirement.
The ESD-protection statement concerns the USB data-line protection device, not power-input ESD protection.
The permanent USBLC6 wiring correction applies to USB data-line ESD protection rather than the target power-input protection Requirement.
The claim concerns AXP2101 exposed-pad thermal handling in the PCB design rather than battery safety protection.
The observed abnormal L3 voltages concern DCDC1 rail regulation rather than battery safety behavior.
The concrete runtime failures concern DCDC1 undervoltage and load-transient collapse rather than battery safety protection.
The statement that the connectors cannot fit within 40 mm primarily reports a board-size and aggregate connector-layout constraint rather than a failure of the battery connector alone.

The freelancer reports an incorrect battery-connector label in a picture; this is direct evidence for connector-label correctness rather than proof that the physical battery-interface pinout was implemented incorrectly.
The message concerns AXP2101 battery overcharge and overdischarge protection rather than the general charge-and-run power-management behavior.
The implementation claim concerns the AXP2101 thermal-pad board design.
The stated expectation concerns operating from USB without a battery, which is owned by the standalone USB power path.
The observed unstable L3 voltage is a concrete failure of DCDC1 output regulation.
The L3 output capacitor short is evidence concerning the DCDC1 output path rather than the broader PMIC selection requirement.
The successful rise of the 3.3V rail verifies only the narrower regulator behavior, not simultaneous charging and full 3.3V/5V power management.
The detailed idle undervoltage, transient collapse, register behavior, and progressive output-stage failure form a DCDC1 regulation trajectory.
The progressive DCDC1 degradation and use of an external 3.3V supply concern the narrower regulator requirement.
Persistence after an attempted AXP2101 replacement is execution evidence for the unresolved DCDC1 failure trajectory.
The abnormal L3 voltage measurements concern DCDC1 rail regulation rather than the standalone LDO and source-ORing path.
The concrete failure in this message is native USB enumeration; the reported 3.3V rail and ESP32 operation do not verify the complete standalone sensor-power behavior.
The incorrectly grounded USBLC6 VBUS pin concerns USB data-line ESD protection.
The confirmed U3 wiring error concerns USB data-line ESD protection.
The terse fix claim is resolvable from context as the USB ESD schematic correction, not the standalone 3.3V power path.
The USB-powered load-transient collapse is specifically attributed to AXP2101 DCDC1 regulation; external 3.3V bypasses that regulator and does not test the standalone LDO path.
The progressive DCDC1 degradation and external-supply workaround concern DCDC1 output regulation.
The report that USB power produced 0V at the sensor pins primarily concerns the USB-powered 3.3V path rather than DCDC1 regulation specifically.
The native USB enumeration failure in this message belongs to the Native USB Programming Requirement; only the explicit 3.3V rail result applies to the target Requirement.
The successful USB enumeration and flashing after removing U3 is execution evidence for Native USB Programming, separate from the DCDC1 observations.
The request to review local DCDC1 VIN input-capacitor placement may affect the separate Power Converter Decoupling Layout Requirement.
The concrete undervoltage, load-transient collapse, and progressive DCDC1 failure observations belong to DCDC1 output regulation; they do not establish that the decoupling layout itself failed.
The reported progressive DCDC1 degradation and external-supply workaround concern regulator behavior rather than a confirmed decoupling-layout failure.
The requested review concerns local input decoupling for the AXP2101 DCDC1 VIN pins, not ESP32 supply-pin decoupling.
In context, the freelancer's claim that the decoupling capacitors are configured properly refers to the AXP2101 DCDC1 input decoupling discussed in message 1046.
The accepted connector price and compatible-alternative constraints concern production component sourceability rather than native USB behavior.
The incorrect USBLC6 pin-5 connection and its clamping effect concern the ESD protection implementation.
The confirmed U3 wiring defect is target-specific evidence for the USB ESD protection Requirement.
The permanent correction separating U3 VBUS and GND while retaining protection belongs to the USB ESD protection Requirement.
The freelancer's commitment to make the permanent U3 correction is an implementation claim for USB ESD protection.
The context-resolved 'Fixed' claim refers to the U3 symbol and net correction, not independently verified native USB operation.
The failure to enumerate or flash is direct execution evidence for native USB programming; the ESD-specific wiring cause is represented separately.
USB operation after removing U3 and bridging the data lines verifies native USB programming, not operation of the ESD protection.
Enumeration and flashing with U3 removed verify the bypassed USB data path and do not verify restored ESD protection.
The claim that every ESP32-S3 module pin is connected to the 40 through-hole pins concerns full pin breakout rather than peripheral GPIO assignment.
The failure to enumerate over native USB belongs to the independently testable native USB programming Requirement.
The traced USBLC6 VBUS-to-GND fault concerns USB data-line ESD protection rather than the general peripheral GPIO map.
The supplied evidence index identifies this pin-order flexibility as applying to the power connector; the source does not explicitly identify the signal connector.
The message uses the existing PWRON signal from J_PWR_SIG to add a separate panel-button connector rather than changing the interboard signal interface.
The message changes physical placement and alignment of the interboard connectors, not their signal content or pinout.
The message primarily establishes that battery charge status is displayed through the SK6812 chain rather than through a separate LED.
The message introduces the separate eight-LED PCB artifact rather than changing its shared electrical interface.
The suspected 3.3V/data pin swap concerns the LED-board connector pinout and is subsequently retracted after inspection.
The confirmation that LED-board pin 1 is 3.3V concerns the physical board connector pinout.
The 5V supply and level-shifter decision concerns shared LED electrical compatibility rather than the LED-board layout artifact.
The LED supply voltage and data-line level-shifter configuration belong to the addressable LED electrical interface.
Independent LED power control and reconsideration of the level shifter concern the electrical interface rather than the LED array board layout.
The change to 3.3V LED power and direct ESP32 data drive belongs to the addressable LED electrical interface.
The request adds an I2C connector for a light sensor rather than changing the e-paper backlight output itself.
This message specifies physical placement and alignment of the separate-board connectors rather than the sensor connector matrix.
This message changes the physical orientation and placement of sensor-board connectors rather than their required functions or pinouts.
The unavailable connectors concern production sourceability rather than whether the connector hub is functionally required.
The missing sensor-board connectors arise in the assembly-order and parts-list context rather than as a change to the connector-hub specification.
This message distinguishes connectors included in the design from their treatment in the BOM, so the evidence belongs to BOM assembly readiness.
The proposed division of the hard-to-source 13-pin connector into separate power and signal connectors primarily changes the interboard interface architecture.
The duplicate part number assigned to capacitors with different values is a BOM accuracy issue rather than a component-sourceability transition.
The statement that the sensor board lacks the connectors concerns connector implementation on that board, not merely sourcing availability.
The unavailable sensor-board connectors are primarily evidence about production component sourceability rather than BOM artifact completeness.
The statement that boards were added to the basket concerns executable PCB order configuration rather than BOM completeness.
This message concerns electrical pin-one numbering and matching interboard pinouts rather than silkscreen connector labels.
The visible dots identify component pin-one orientation rather than connector pin-function labels.
The reported incorrectly rotated components concern assembly-orientation validation rather than general order configuration.
The client's inability to determine correct rotations in the assembly preview concerns component-orientation validation.
The request for a lower-cost connector alternative concerns component sourceability and minimum-order risk.
The unchanged connector price and minimum quantity are sourceability evidence rather than an order-configuration failure.
Checking whether components receive JLCPCB Basic classification primarily concerns production component sourceability.
The request to verify component orientation belongs to the dedicated assembly-orientation Requirement.
The question about relocating pins and AXP IRQ concerns GPIO allocation rather than the sleep-policy values established by the same message.
The boost EN question concerns control of the switched 5V rail rather than ESP32 sleep and wake behavior.
The proposed pull-down on the boost converter EN pin concerns the switched 5V rail's default-off behavior.
The implementation claim reports a VBACKUP header and VRTC output but does not report adding PWROK access.
The proposed BOOT and EN capacitor change concerns the reset/boot circuitry rather than the panel GPIO button and switch inputs.
The client's acceptance of 1uF BOOT and EN capacitors concerns the reset/boot circuitry rather than this target Requirement.

The factory's failure to bake moisture-sensitive AXP2101 parts before reflow and its plan to bake them for production concern pre-reflow moisture handling rather than thermal-pad or stencil implementation.
The proposed segmented thermal-pad paste aperture concerns stencil and thermal-pad implementation rather than pre-reflow moisture handling.
The concrete runtime observations concern DCDC1 undervoltage and load-transient collapse; moisture damage is only one unconfirmed possible cause.

missing_requirement_candidates.description: The sensor board has a separate component-fit problem and subsequent completion claim. This trajectory is independent of the main-board form-factor Requirement and is not represented by a suitable frozen Requirement.
The evidence defines deep-sleep conditions and timer/touch wake sources as independently evolving power-management behavior not represented by the frozen inventory.

After the project shifts to a single integrated board, the client requests additional sensor-facing JST/I2C connectors. These changes do not safely apply to the separately defined sensor-board connector hub, and no current Requirement specifically owns the integrated board's sensor connector matrix.
